title: "Erik Brynjolfsson"

**Erik Brynjolfsson** (b. 1962) directs Stanford's Digital Economy Lab (previously head of
MIT's Initiative on the Digital Economy) and is the most prominent voice on the economics of
information technology and AI. With Andrew McAfee he wrote *The Second Machine Age*; with
Daniel Rock and Chad Syverson he formalized David's insight for the AI era as the
*Productivity J-Curve* (2018) — general-purpose technologies demand large, poorly-measured
intangible investments, so productivity looks worse than reality early and better later. A
techno-realist: bullish on the upside, insistent that the distributional outcome is a
*choice*, not a property of the technology.
